title: A quasi-coherent module on a qcqs scheme is a filtered colimit of modules of finite presentation, indexed by a filtered category (Stacks 01PJ)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Then there exist a small filtered category $\mathcal I$ (its objects form a set; it is nonempty, any two objects $i,i'$ admit morphisms $i\to i''$, $i'\to i''$ to a common object, and any two parallel morphisms $a,b:i\to i'$ are equalized by some $c:i'\to i''$, $ca=cb$) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a functor $M:\mathcal I\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$, with every $\mathcal F_i$ of finite presentation, and $\mathcal O_X$-module maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ M(a)=\varphi_i$ for every morphism $a:i\to i'$ of $\mathcal I$, such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $M$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ (lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, line 3040); its proof uses Modules, Lemma 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), direct sums and cokernels of finitely presented modules, stalks of colimits (Sheaves, Section 009E), Properties, Lemma 01PF (lemma-extend, line 2847) and Lemma 01PI (lemma-extend-finite-presentation, line 2924)

proof.text: Choose a set $I$ of pairs $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_i)$, where $\mathcal F_i$ is of finite presentation and $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$, containing a representative of every such pair up to isomorphism over $\mathcal F$. This is possible by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-representatives]: finite-presentation modules form a set up to isomorphism, and each Hom collection is a set. Make $I$ a category by taking morphisms $i\to i'$ to be maps $a:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'}$ satisfying $\varphi_{i'}a=\varphi_i$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ proof, first paragraph (lines 3060-3069), using Modules 01BC

proof.text: The category $I$ is nonempty (use the zero module). Given $i,i'$, the map $\mathcal F_i\oplus\mathcal F_{i'}\to\mathcal F$ induced by $\varphi_i,\varphi_{i'}$ has finite-presentation source by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-direct-sum], hence is isomorphic over $\mathcal F$ to some chosen pair $(\mathcal F_{i''},\varphi_{i''})$; the two summand inclusions give morphisms $i\to i''$ and $i'\to i''$.

For parallel $a,b:i\to i'$, put $\mathcal G=\operatorname{Coker}(a-b)$. It is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel]. Since $\varphi_{i'}a=\varphi_i=\varphi_{i'}b$, $\varphi_{i'}$ factors through $\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$; representing this pair by some $i''$ gives a morphism $i'\to i''$ equalizing $a,b$. Thus $I$ is filtered.

The maps $\varphi_i$ form a cocone, hence induce $\varphi:\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-filtered-colimit], its stalk at $x$ is the map $\varinjlim_i(\mathcal F_i)_x\to\mathcal F_x$. To prove that $\varphi$ is an isomorphism it suffices to prove these stalk maps bijective, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ proof, fourth paragraph (lines 3119-3131); Sheaves Section 009E

proof.text: For injectivity, let $s\in(\mathcal F_i)_x$ map to zero in $\mathcal F_x$. On a quasi-compact neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, represent $s$ by a section still denoted $s$ with $\varphi_i(s)=0$. The cyclic image $\mathcal K_U=\operatorname{Im}(\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{1\mapsto s}\mathcal F_i|_U)$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule: quasi-coherence and the identification with the image sheaf follow from [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], and finite type follows because it is a quotient of $\mathcal O_U$ by its kernel. Since $\mathcal K_U\subseteq\ker(\varphi_i)|_U$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-submodule-extension] extends it to a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal K\subseteq\ker(\varphi_i)$. The quotient map $\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_i/\mathcal K$ has finite-presentation source and target quotient by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel], and its induced map to $\mathcal F$ is represented by some $i'$. The resulting transition $i\to i'$ kills $s$, so the class of $s$ vanishes in $\varinjlim_i(\mathcal F_i)_x$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ proof, injectivity paragraph (lines 3132-3162), using Lemma 01PF

proof.text: For surjectivity, take $s\in\mathcal F_x$ and represent it on a quasi-compact neighbourhood $U$ by $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, equivalently by the map $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal F|_U$, $1\mapsto s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-extension], this map extends to $\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal G$ of finite presentation on $X$. Represent the pair by some $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_i)$; the section $1$ over $U$ gives a germ in $(\mathcal F_i)_x$ mapping to $s$. Hence every stalk map is surjective.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ proof, surjectivity paragraph (lines 3163-3187), using Lemma 01PI

proof.text: Steps 5 and 6 show every stalk of $\varphi$ is bijective, so Step 4 gives that $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Transporting the canonical colimit cocone across this isomorphism makes $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_i)_i)$ a colimit of the filtered diagram, as required.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks 01PJ into seven steps: choose a small representative category, prove its two filteredness conditions using finite direct sums and cokernels, identify the colimit stalkwise, prove injectivity using the existing quasi-coherent image theorem and 01PF, prove surjectivity using 01PI, and conclude by stalkwise detection of isomorphisms. Created six public child nodes for the reusable non-elementary inputs; reused the existing stalkwise-isomorphism and quasi-coherent-image nodes.
